questions.q: Why does the summary say education must become a continuous part of life?
a: Skills have to adapt as technology and jobs keep changing
Degrees become more expensive with each passing year
Employers increasingly prefer younger applicants
Retirement ages are falling in most countries
questions.why: The overview argues that the old path of a degree followed by one career is outdated because work keeps changing.

questions.q: What do workers over 50 need, according to the summary?
a: Training matched to their skills and market demand
Early retirement packages and larger pensions
Shorter hours and much lighter duties
A return to full-time university study
questions.why: The first lesson says older workers are not leaving the workforce but need training aligned with their skills and demand.

questions.q: What does the learning-by-doing approach involve?
a: Learning on the job through targeted training programs
Studying full time before ever entering the workforce
Taking evening courses in unrelated subjects
Reading textbooks and attending lectures only
questions.why: The second lesson recommends training programs designed around needed skills, plus on-ramps that place adults into local work.

questions.q: What is credential inflation, as the summary describes it?
a: Employers demand higher degrees, so applicants keep adding qualifications
Rising tuition makes every degree less valuable over time
Too many graduates compete for too few available jobs
Companies invent certificates to attract more workers
questions.why: The third lesson says employers now require advanced degrees instead of treating them as extras, so applicants pile up credentials.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend instead of judging applicants by credentials?
a: Performance-based assessments and skills-based resumes
Longer degree programs with deeper specialization
Interviews run by outside consultants
Standardized tests taken before applying
questions.why: It suggests Collegiate Learning Assessments built on a 90-minute practical task, plus resumes that show actual skills.
